{{Short description|French chemist (born 1955)}}
{{BLP primary sources|date=August 2019}}
'''Paul Knochel''' (born 15 November 1955) is a French [[chemist]] and a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]].

== Biography ==
Paul Knochel was born in [[Strasbourg]]. He studied chemistry at the [[University technical institute (France)|university technical institute]] (IUT) in Strasbourg, then at the ENSCS (École Nationale Supérieure de Chimie de Strasbourg). From 1979 to 1982, he completed his thesis entitled "Nitroallyl-halogenide und -ester als effiziente Verknüpfungsreagenzien" at [[ETH Zurich]] (Switzerland) in the group of [[Dieter Seebach]]. He then spent four years at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS) at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University|Pierre et Marie Curie University]] in [[Paris]] in the group of Jean-François Normant. During this period, he studied carbozincation reactions using [[allylic]] reagents and prepared [[Organometallic|bimetallic]] compounds bearing two different metals ([[Lithium]], [[Magnesium]] or [[Zinc]]) on the same carbon atom. He then joined [[Martin F. Semmelhack]]'s laboratory for a [[Postdoctoral researcher|post-doctoral]] fellowship during which he worked on the use of [[indole]]s-[[chromium]] complexes in organic synthesis. In 1987, he accepted a position as [[Assistant professor|Assistant Professor]] in the Department of Chemistry at the [[University of Michigan]] at [[Ann Arbor, Michigan|Ann Arbor]] (MI, USA) where he developed the first methods for the preparation of polyfunctional [[Organometallic chemistry|organometallic]] zinc species. In 1991, he was promoted to [[Professor]] at the same university before moving to [[Marburg University]] (Germany) in 1992, where he was offered a position as Professor of [[Organic chemistry|Organic Chemistry]] in the Department of Chemistry at Marburg University. He continued his work on the chemistry of polyfunctional organozinciques and their use in [[asymmetric synthesis]]. In 1999, he was offered a position as Professor of Organic Chemistry at [[LMU Munich]]<ref name="Group of Prof. Paul Knochel 2021">{{cite web | title=Prof. Paul Knochel {{!}} Curriculum Vitae | website=Group of Prof. Paul Knochel {{!}} Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München | date=16 December 2021 | url=http://www.knochel.cup.uni-muenchen.de/prof-dr-paul-knochel/curriculum-vitae/ | access-date=16 December 2021}}</ref><ref name="Faculty for Chemistry and Pharmacy LMU Munich">{{cite web | title=Prof. Dr. Paul Knochel | website=Faculty for Chemistry and Pharmacy LMU Munich | url=https://www.cup.lmu.de/en/departments/chemistry/people/prof-dr-paul-knochel/ | access-date=16 December 2021}}</ref> which he still holds in 2019. He has developed new methods for the preparation of polyfunctional organometallic species as well as numerous synthetic methods using organometallic reagents or catalysts.

== Scientific work ==
Knochel has developed a series of new methods for the preparation of polyfunctional organometallic species of zinc<ref name="Ellwart Knochel pp. 10662–10665">{{cite journal | last1=Ellwart | first1=Mario | last2=Knochel | first2=Paul | title=Preparation of Solid, Substituted Allylic Zinc Reagents and Their Reactions with Electrophiles | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition | publisher=Wiley | volume=54 | issue=36 | date=17 July 2015 | issn=1433-7851 | doi=10.1002/anie.201504354 | pages=10662–10665| pmid=26189654 }}</ref> and magnesium, but also many other metals such as [[copper]], [[aluminium]],<ref name="Blümke Chen Peng Knochel pp. 313–318">{{cite journal | last1=Blümke | first1=Tobias | last2=Chen | first2=Yi-Hung | last3=Peng | first3=Zhihua | last4=Knochel | first4=Paul | title=Preparation of functionalized organoaluminiums by direct insertion of aluminium to unsaturated halides | journal=Nature Chemistry | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=2 | issue=4 | date=24 March 2010 | issn=1755-4330 | doi=10.1038/nchem.590 | pages=313–318| pmid=21124514 | bibcode=2010NatCh...2..313B | s2cid=5280421 }}</ref> [[manganese]], [[indium]], [[iron]], [[lanthanum]] and [[samarium]]. In addition, he highlighted the fact that lithium salts catalyse a significant number of organometallic reactions, including the oxidative addition of a metal such as magnesium,<ref name="Krasovskiy Knochel pp. 3333–3336">{{cite journal | last1=Krasovskiy | first1=Arkady | last2=Knochel | first2=Paul | title=A LiCl-Mediated Br/Mg Exchange Reaction for the Preparation of Functionalized Aryl- and Heteroarylmagnesium Compounds from Organic Bromides | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition | publisher=Wiley | volume=43 | issue=25 | date=21 June 2004 | issn=1433-7851 | doi=10.1002/anie.200454084 | pages=3333–3336| pmid=15213967 }}</ref> zinc,<ref name="Krasovskiy Malakhov Gavryushin Knochel pp. 6040–6044">{{cite journal | last1=Krasovskiy | first1=Arkady | last2=Malakhov | first2=Vladimir | last3=Gavryushin | first3=Andrei | last4=Knochel | first4=Paul | title=Efficient Synthesis of Functionalized Organozinc Compounds by the Direct Insertion of Zinc into Organic Iodides and Bromides | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition | publisher=Wiley | volume=45 | issue=36 | date=11 September 2006 | issn=1433-7851 | doi=10.1002/anie.200601450 | pages=6040–6044| pmid=16900548 }}</ref> indium, manganese or aluminium to an organic [[halide]]. It has shown that the use of [[lithium]] derivatives ([[chloride]], [[acetylacetonates]] or [[alcoholate]]s)<ref name="Kneisel Dochnahl Knochel pp. 1017–1021">{{cite journal | last1=Kneisel | first1=Florian F. | last2=Dochnahl | first2=Maximilian | last3=Knochel | first3=Paul | title=Nucleophilic Catalysis of the Iodine–Zinc Exchange Reaction: Preparation of Highly Functionalized Diaryl Zinc Compounds | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition | publisher=Wiley | volume=43 | issue=8 | date=13 February 2004 | issn=1433-7851 | doi=10.1002/anie.200353316 | pages=1017–1021| pmid=14966896 }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite journal | last1=Ziegler | first1=Dorothée S. | last2=Karaghiosoff | first2=Konstantin | last3=Knochel | first3=Paul | title=Generation of Aryl and Heteroaryl Magnesium Reagents in Toluene by Br/Mg or Cl/Mg Exchange | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition | publisher=Wiley | volume=57 | issue=22 | date=28 May 2018 | issn=1433-7851 | doi=10.1002/anie.201802123 | pages=6701–6704| pmid=29656503 }}</ref> catalyses the halogen-metal exchange in the preparation of organomagnesians<ref name=":0" /> and organozinciques. In addition, it has synthesized a series of new cluttered metal bases derived from [[2,2,6,6-Tetramethylpiperidine|tetramethylpiperidine]] allowing C-H activations of [[Aromatic hydrocarbon|aromatic]] and [[Heterocyclic compound|heterocyclic]] unsaturated systems.<ref name="Makarov Brocklehurst Karaghiosoff Koch pp. 12774–12777">{{cite journal | last1=Makarov | first1=Ilya S. | last2=Brocklehurst |
